_comment: Curated seed events for the Atlas. Editorial layer: written/approved by the Republic. sourceCluster here links only to stable institutional references (no fabricated articles). Auto-collected news lives in live.json. Status workflow: auto_collected -> needs_review -> curated -> published.

events.title: Drifter Constellation
events.summary: Live drifting sensing node operating between Malta and Lampedusa. Position updates reflect environmental drift and transmission conditions.
events.whatHappened: The Republic maintains an autonomous drifting buoy constellation in the central Mediterranean: GNSS, solar-assisted power, interval telemetry. The same waters crossed by migration routes, SAR operations and surveillance assets are sensed by a stateless object.
events.republicReading: The Drifter occupies the gap between sensing and being sensed. In a sea saturated with radar, AIS and aerial patrol, a drifting object with no flag and no cargo is almost illegible — which is exactly the point.

events.title: Embassy
events.summary: A mobile diplomatic fiction unit: an access point to a stateless institution, turning places into temporary jurisdictions.
events.whatHappened: Embassy is a roaming protocol — a rover that produces proximity, negotiation and friction, inviting visitors to navigate thresholds as if they were borders.
events.republicReading: Where states project embassies as fixed stone, the Republic deploys one as a vehicle. Jurisdiction becomes a parking question.

events.title: Liability
events.summary: An AI interlocutor that manipulates bias and mediates between people and devices — a seductive layer of governance.
events.whatHappened: Liability redirects attention, reframes choices, and turns interaction into a negotiation about agency, control and responsibility.
events.republicReading: The Atlas compares narrative frames produced by media regions; Liability produces them synthetically, one conversation at a time. Same machinery, different scale.

events.title: Treasury
events.summary: A speculation engine for a remote node: distance becomes a financial interface, location a contested variable.
events.whatHappened: Treasury frames infrastructure as a narrative substrate where value, movement and risk are continuously re-authored.
events.republicReading: Ports price distance; Treasury prices the idea of distance. Both are speculative instruments built on the same desert logistics.

events.title: Red Sea diversion regime: the long detour as new normal
events.summary: Since late 2023, attacks on commercial shipping around Bab el-Mandeb have pushed a large share of container traffic onto the Cape of Good Hope route, restructuring global schedules, insurance and port loads. The situation remains fluid.
events.whatHappened: Armed attacks and seizures targeting commercial vessels in the southern Red Sea triggered mass rerouting around Africa. Transit volumes through the Suez system fell sharply; war-risk insurance, bunkering patterns and African port congestion shifted with them. Episodes of partial return alternate with new disruptions.

sourceCluster.title: IMO — maritime security
sourceCluster.excerpt: Institutional reference for shipping security advisories.

west.frame: Supply-chain disruption, freight inflation, naval coalition framing: the strait as a security corridor to be re-opened.

east.frame: Exposure of China- and India-bound flows, energy routing, opportunity framing for alternative corridors and rail.

south.frame: Cape route windfall and burden: South African port congestion, bunker demand, freight costs passed to import-dependent economies.

mena.frame: Sovereignty and war-spillover framing: the strait as leverage, regional escalation risk, Egypt's canal revenues as collateral damage.

local.frame: Yemeni coastal communities between blockade, strikes and fishing grounds turned into a frontline.

events.republicReading: A chokepoint is a narrative device: one strait can re-price the planet. The diversion regime shows that the global supply chain has a geography of fear — and that whoever can make a strait feel unsafe holds a kind of sovereignty no flag recognises.

events.title: Suez Canal revenues as a seismograph of distant wars
events.summary: Canal transit revenues — a structural pillar of Egypt's foreign-currency income — collapsed with the Red Sea crisis and have oscillated with every shift in strait security since, entangling Egyptian fiscal policy with events it does not control.
events.whatHappened: Following mass rerouting from late 2023, Suez Canal Authority receipts fell steeply. Recovery has tracked the perceived safety of Bab el-Mandeb rather than any decision made in Cairo, exposing how a national budget can be hostage to a strait 1,500 km away.

sourceCluster.title: Suez Canal Authority — official statistics
sourceCluster.excerpt: Primary institutional source for transit and revenue figures.

west.frame: Macro-stability story: IMF programs, currency risk, Egypt as too-big-to-fail borrower.

east.frame: Corridor competition story: alternative routes, investment diplomacy, multipolar leverage over Cairo.

south.frame: Debt-dependency story: what a revenue shock means for subsidies, food imports and the Egyptian pound.

mena.frame: Sovereignty story: the canal as national symbol whose income is set by foreign wars and foreign insurers.

local.frame: Canal cities (Port Said, Ismailia, Suez) where transit work, pilotage and services absorb the shock first.

events.republicReading: The canal is the Republic's namesake and its core paradox: a strip of national territory whose value is set entirely by transnational flows. When revenues fall, the fiction of sovereign infrastructure becomes visible as fiction.

events.title: Central Mediterranean: rescue as a contested jurisdiction
events.summary: The sea between Libya, Tunisia, Malta and Italy remains the world's most lethal migration route. NGO rescue vessels operate inside a shifting legal architecture of distant ports, detention decrees and contested SAR zones.
events.whatHappened: Crossings and deaths continue along the central route. Italian regulations assign distant disembarkation ports and detain rescue vessels over administrative infractions; Libyan and Tunisian coast guards, partly EU-funded, intercept and return people. The SAR zone itself — a technical artifact of maritime law — functions as a political instrument.

sourceCluster.excerpt: Arrivals, dead and missing: primary statistical reference.

sourceCluster.title: IOM — Missing Migrants Project
sourceCluster.excerpt: Documentation of deaths along migration routes.

west.frame: Border-management framing: flows, smuggling networks, electoral pressure, externalisation deals presented as stabilisation.

east.frame: Often covered as a European governance failure; occasionally instrumentalised in geopolitical messaging.

south.frame: Departure-country framing: remittances, youth unemployment, the route as survival economics rather than crisis.

mena.frame: Transit framing: Libya and Tunisia as pressured gatekeepers, EU funds as leverage, sovereignty traded for border enforcement.

local.frame: Lampedusa, Zarzis, coastal Malta: reception infrastructure, fishing communities recovering bodies and boats.

events.republicReading: SAR zones are the purest case of cartography as power: invisible rectangles at sea deciding who rescues, who returns, who counts the dead. The Republic's Drifter floats in exactly these waters — sensing a sea that is legally four different seas at once.

events.title: Undersea cables in the Red Sea corridor: bandwidth follows shipping lanes
events.summary: Cable damage incidents in the Red Sea corridor (notably early 2024) degraded Europe–Asia internet capacity and exposed how digital traffic is funnelled through the same chokepoint as container ships.
events.whatHappened: Multiple submarine cable systems running the Red Sea corridor suffered cuts during the shipping crisis, with traffic rerouted at capacity cost. Repair operations in contested waters require permits, security guarantees and specialised ships — a reminder that the cloud has a draft depth.

sourceCluster.title: Submarine Cable Map
sourceCluster.excerpt: Reference map of cable systems transiting the Red Sea corridor.

west.frame: Resilience and threat framing: critical infrastructure protection, suspicion of deliberate targeting.

east.frame: Capacity and routing framing: Asia–Europe latency, alternative terrestrial corridors through different sovereignties.

south.frame: Dependency framing: East African connectivity riding on cables it neither owns nor repairs.

mena.frame: Jurisdiction framing: repair permits as leverage, territorial waters as bargaining chips.

local.frame: Outage framing: degraded service in Yemen, Djibouti, Sudan measured in hours of disconnection.

events.republicReading: The homepage of this very site draws these cables as thin violet lines. When they are cut, the Atlas itself becomes slower to load in three continents — the rare case where the map is materially inside its own territory.

events.title: Mediterranean marine heatwaves: the sea as a warming archive
events.summary: Successive summers have set Mediterranean sea-surface temperature records, with marine heatwaves restructuring fisheries, intensifying storms and changing what the sea is for the people who work it.
events.whatHappened: Satellite monitoring shows recurring basin-wide marine heatwave conditions in recent summers. Warmer water loads the atmosphere for extreme rain events, stresses fisheries and aquaculture, and shifts species ranges — a slow event that only becomes news when it produces a flood.

sourceCluster.title: Copernicus Marine — SST monitoring
sourceCluster.excerpt: Primary satellite reference for Mediterranean sea-surface temperature.

west.frame: Climate-impact framing: records, attribution science, tourism and insurance exposure.

east.frame: Sparse coverage; mostly via global climate reporting.

south.frame: Livelihood framing: artisanal fisheries and food security on the southern shore.

mena.frame: Water and coast framing: desalination, coastal cities, agricultural stress feeding migration pressure.

local.frame: Fishing ports noticing the catch change before any bulletin names it.

events.republicReading: The Republic's own data pipeline (Currents) renders this sea as flowing vectors. A marine heatwave is an event with no coordinates and every coordinate — the limit case for any atlas that claims to map events as points.

events.title: Shadow fleets: sanctioned oil and the politics of looking away
events.summary: Aging tankers with opaque ownership move sanctioned crude through the Mediterranean and adjacent seas, using flag-hopping, AIS gaps and ship-to-ship transfers. Their visibility is itself a political negotiation.
events.whatHappened: Since the tightening of oil sanctions, a parallel tanker economy has grown: vessels beyond mainstream insurance, transferring cargo at sea, going dark on transponders. Enforcement attention moves between the Baltic, the Aegean and the Gulf depending on the diplomatic weather.

sourceCluster.title: Global Fishing Watch — vessel transparency research
sourceCluster.excerpt: Open data on AIS gaps and dark vessel behaviour (methodological reference).

west.frame: Enforcement framing: sanctions evasion, environmental time-bombs, insurance loopholes to be closed.

east.frame: Trade-continuity framing: discounted energy flows, sanctions as Western overreach, alternative shipping ecosystems.

south.frame: Price framing: what discounted crude and its risks mean for importing economies.

mena.frame: Transit framing: straits and bunkering hubs profiting quietly from flows nobody officially sees.

local.frame: Coastal communities living next to uninsured tankers doing ship-to-ship transfers offshore.

events.republicReading: The shadow fleet is the inverse of the Atlas: infrastructure that works by not being mapped. Every AIS gap is a small stateless territory — proof that invisibility at sea is manufactured, priced and sold.

events.title: Remote warfare over shipping lanes: drones as the new weather

location.name: Southern Red Sea / Gulf of Aden

events.summary: Cheap one-way drones and anti-ship missiles, intercepted by warships and carrier aircraft, have turned the Red Sea corridor into a laboratory of asymmetric remote warfare — fought largely by machines over the heads of commercial crews.
events.whatHappened: Recurrent drone and missile launches against shipping, met by multinational naval interception operations, have normalised a low-intensity machine war along the corridor. The economics are inverted: interceptors cost orders of magnitude more than what they shoot down.

sourceCluster.title: ACLED — conflict event data
sourceCluster.excerpt: Structured conflict event dataset covering Red Sea attacks (future ingest integration).

west.frame: Freedom-of-navigation framing: naval coalitions, interception successes, deterrence vocabulary.

east.frame: Quagmire framing: Western naval overstretch, regional blowback, parallel diplomatic tracks.

south.frame: Cost framing: insurance and freight premiums exported to economies far from the launch sites.

mena.frame: Solidarity-and-leverage framing: strikes narrated as pressure politics, civilian toll of retaliation.

local.frame: Crews and coastal villages under flight paths — the only humans physically present in a machine conflict.

events.republicReading: Remote warfare makes the chokepoint recursive: the strait is attacked remotely, defended remotely, narrated remotely. The only bodies on site are seafarers — mostly from the Global South — whose names appear in no frame.

links.relation: investigate: who built and sold what is flying

events.title: Arms flows and accountability: every strike has a supply chain
events.summary: Behind each attack and each interception in the Red Sea corridor sits a documented trail: export licenses, transfer registers, sanctions panel reports and procurement contracts. The Atlas reads strikes backwards — from the explosion to the invoice.
events.whatHappened: Public registers document the flows feeding the corridor war: SIPRI's Arms Transfers Database tracks deliveries of missiles, drones and naval systems by supplier and recipient; UN Panel of Experts reports document component provenance in intercepted weapons; EU member-state export license reports list approvals to the coalition navies' suppliers; national procurement databases publish the interceptor contracts. None of this is secret — it is distributed across formats designed not to be read together.

west.frame: Procurement framing: replenishment budgets, industrial-base capacity, interceptor cost curves debated as policy.

east.frame: Hypocrisy framing: Western export volumes contrasted with sanctions rhetoric; alternative suppliers normalised.

south.frame: Recipient framing: arms inflows as debt, leverage and conflict fuel in economies that import security.

mena.frame: Patronage framing: transfers as alliance currency, end-use conditions as sovereignty disputes.

local.frame: Component framing: serial numbers recovered from wreckage tracing a global factory floor to one village.

events.republicReading: An explosion is the last line of a contract. The Atlas treats arms registers as cartography: every transfer row is an arc between two countries that will eventually land somewhere as a coordinate. Accountability is a mapping problem before it is a legal one.

events.title: Ukraine eastern front: Donetsk grinding war
events.summary: Attritional warfare continues along the Donetsk contact line with daily artillery exchanges, drone strikes and incremental territorial shifts.
events.whatHappened: Russian forces maintain pressure across the Donetsk front with artillery superiority; Ukrainian lines hold with combined drone-infantry tactics and Western-supplied munitions.

events.title: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant under military control
events.summary: The world's largest nuclear plant remains under Russian military occupation; IAEA monitoring missions report ongoing violations of nuclear safety principles.
events.whatHappened: Armed forces present on site, external power supply intermittent, cooling systems under stress. IAEA maintains resident presence but access constrained.

events.title: Cross-border strikes: Belgorod and Russian border regions
events.summary: Ukrainian forces and affiliated groups conduct periodic strikes into Belgorod oblast; drone campaigns target oil facilities, radar and logistics nodes.
events.whatHappened: Cross-border incursions and drone strikes have forced Russian border-region evacuations; attacks on oil refineries and ammunition depots continued through 2025-26.

events.title: Gaza: siege, displacement and urban annihilation
events.summary: Israeli military campaign following the October 7 attacks has caused mass civilian casualties, displacement of over 1.7 million and near-total destruction of northern Gaza.
events.whatHappened: IDF ground and air operations reduced much of Gaza City and north Gaza to rubble; humanitarian corridors contested; ceasefire negotiations repeatedly collapse; south Gaza and Rafah subsequently targeted.

events.title: West Bank: settler raids and military annexation creep
events.summary: Settler violence and IDF operations in the West Bank accelerated after October 7; Area C expansion and road seizures advance effective annexation.
events.whatHappened: Coordinated settler raids on Palestinian villages accompanied by IDF protection; Palestinian fatalities at multi-decade highs; outpost legalisation undermines two-state framework.

events.title: Sudan: RSF vs SAF — civil war inside the capital
events.summary: Rapid Support Forces and Sudanese Armed Forces have fought for control of Khartoum since April 2023 in one of the world's most underreported urban wars.
events.whatHappened: RSF controls large parts of Khartoum and Omdurman; SAF retains northern and eastern positions; infrastructure destroyed, millions displaced, humanitarian corridors blocked.

events.title: Darfur: ethnic massacres resume under RSF
events.summary: RSF-linked militias have resumed systematic attacks on Masalit and other non-Arab communities in West Darfur; El-Fasher under siege.
events.whatHappened: Thousands killed in El-Geneina and surrounding areas; ICJ and ICC proceedings active; UN Panel documents ethnic-cleansing patterns consistent with genocide.

events.title: Myanmar: junta airstrikes on civilian populations
events.summary: Tatmadaw airstrikes on villages and resistance-held towns continue; ethnic resistance armies and PDF forces control increasing territory.
events.whatHappened: Three Brotherhood Alliance offensive (Operation 1027) captured multiple towns in late 2023; junta responds with air bombardment of civilian infrastructure; over 2 million internally displaced.

events.title: Mali: jihadist expansion and Wagner presence
events.summary: JNIM and ISGS expand territorial control across the Sahel; Malian junta relies on Russian Wagner/Africa Corps presence; French forces expelled.
events.whatHappened: Attacks on civilians and security forces accelerate; UN MINUSMA withdrawn; Russia/Africa Corps fill void; humanitarian corridors to the north cut.

events.title: Burkina Faso: junta, jihadists and AES bloc
events.summary: Junta government under Traore tightens grip; JNIM controls 40%+ of territory; humanitarian blockades in north and east.
events.whatHappened: Military junta expelled French forces, joined AES bloc with Mali and Niger; internet shutdowns during offensives; siege of Djibo cut off hundreds of thousands.

events.title: Nigeria: Boko Haram and ISWAP in Lake Chad basin
events.summary: ISWAP controls substantial territory around Lake Chad; periodic mass casualty attacks on military and civilian targets in Borno and Yobe.
events.whatHappened: ISWAP attacks on military convoys and aid workers continue; Nigerian army operations have limited but not stopped insurgent activity; over 2 million IDPs in northeast.

events.title: Somalia: Al-Shabaab — resilient insurgency
events.summary: Al-Shabaab retains control of large rural areas and conducts attacks in Mogadishu; ATMIS drawdown threatens hard-won gains.
events.whatHappened: SNA and ATMIS forces recaptured towns in 2022-23; Al-Shabaab counter-attacks and sieges followed; US drone strikes ongoing; ATMIS withdrawal schedule disputed.

events.title: DRC: M23/Rwanda advance in eastern Congo
events.summary: M23 rebels backed by Rwanda seized Goma and Bukavu in early 2025; SADC and UN forces unable to contain advance; mineral control central to conflict.
events.whatHappened: M23 with Rwandan support captured North and South Kivu capitals; humanitarian catastrophe with 7+ million displaced; ICC and UN Group of Experts document Rwanda's role.

events.title: Mozambique: jihadist insurgency, Cabo Delgado
events.summary: Ansar al-Sunna/ISWAP-affiliated insurgency controls Mocímboa da Praia corridor; threatens Total Energies LNG mega-project.
events.whatHappened: RWANDAN and SAMIM forces partially restored security; LNG project suspended; over 1 million displaced; insurgent attacks on villages continue.

events.title: Haiti: gang federations control Port-au-Prince
events.summary: Viv Ansanm gang coalition controls 80%+ of Port-au-Prince; Kenya-led Multinational Security Support mission struggles with mandate and logistics.
events.whatHappened: Gangs forced PM resignation March 2024; MSS forces deployed but with limited reach; humanitarian crisis with food insecurity at famine-adjacent levels.

events.title: Philippines: NPA-CPP guerrilla war, Mindanao
events.summary: NPA guerrillas maintain active operations in Mindanao and Visayas despite AFP counterinsurgency campaigns; peace talks repeatedly collapse.
events.whatHappened: AFP operations continue with drone surveillance and ground clearing; NPA retaliatory attacks on mining and agricultural infrastructure; localised displacement.

events.title: Ethiopia: Amhara conflict and federal fragmentation
events.summary: Federal government conflict with Fano militias in Amhara continues; Tigray ceasefire holds but TPLF disarmament incomplete; Oromia low-level conflict ongoing.
events.whatHappened: Internet shutdowns, mass arrests and airstrikes in Amhara following government disarmament drive; Tigray transitional justice process stalled; OLA operations continue.

events.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran tanker seizures and naval pressure
events.summary: IRGCN periodic seizures and harassment of commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz continue as leverage in nuclear negotiations.
events.whatHappened: Multiple tanker seizures and boardings; US and allied naval presence increased; Iran uses chokepoint threats as diplomatic signalling; 20% of global oil supply transits daily.

events.title: South China Sea: PRC coast guard and PLA-N operations
events.summary: PRC coast guard water cannon attacks on Philippine resupply missions at Second Thomas Shoal; PLA-N exercises encircle Taiwan periodically.
events.whatHappened: PLAN and coast guard ships block and confront Philippine vessels; US-Philippines mutual defence treaty invoked rhetorically; ASEAN unity fragmented over South China Sea code of conduct.

events.title: Malacca Strait: traffic surge post-Suez rerouting
events.summary: Partial Red Sea rerouting shifted additional traffic through Malacca; Singapore and Port Klang see record throughput; chokepoint vulnerability discussed.
events.whatHappened: Congestion at anchorages increased; port call wait times extended; piracy incidents in the strait remain low relative to historical average but increase in Malacca approaches.

events.title: Cape of Good Hope: African ports under rerouting pressure

location.name: Cape of Good Hope, South Africa

events.summary: Mass Suez rerouting adds 3,000–4,000 nautical miles per voyage; South African ports congested; bunker demand spike reshapes ship economics.
events.whatHappened: Transnet port delays worsened by infrastructure problems; shipping lines absorbed cost through slow steaming and vessel pooling; South Africa gains bunkering revenue.

events.title: Arctic Northern Sea Route: melting opens contested passage
events.summary: Arctic warming extends the NSR navigation window; Russia controls access and fees; NATO and China contest governance of the polar sea.
events.whatHappened: Record transits through NSR; Russia requires icebreaker escort and advance notice; China's Polar Silk Road investments continue; US and Canadian Arctic sovereignty claims contested.

events.title: Panama Canal: drought restricts draft depths
events.summary: Severe drought reduced Gatun Lake levels forcing draft restrictions on Panama Canal transits; LNG and container traffic queued for weeks.
events.whatHappened: Draft restrictions cut maximum transit cargo by ~36%; daily transits reduced from 36–38 to 22–24; shipping backlog stretched over 100 vessels; shippers sought alternate routes.

events.title: Taiwan Strait: PLA encirclement exercises
events.summary: PLA conducts periodic large-scale encirclement exercises around Taiwan; live-fire drills shut shipping lanes; US carrier groups transit in response.
events.whatHappened: Multiple exercises following Pelosi visit (2022), Lai Ching-te inauguration (2024) and other political triggers; PLA declares exclusion zones blocking international shipping temporarily.

events.title: Black Sea: Ukrainian naval drone campaign vs Russian fleet
events.summary: Ukraine's uncrewed surface vessel campaign has degraded Russian Black Sea Fleet and forced partial withdrawal from Sevastopol; grain corridor remains contested.
events.whatHappened: Multiple Russian warships sunk or damaged by USV strikes; Black Sea Fleet flagship Moskva sunk 2022; naval drone attacks continue on Crimea-based assets; grain export corridor established then collapsed.

events.title: Gulf of Guinea: piracy and offshore platform attacks
events.summary: Gulf of Guinea remains highest-risk piracy zone globally; crew kidnapping for ransom targets vessels in the Nigerian EEZ and beyond.
events.whatHappened: IMB reports periodic high-profile kidnappings; Benin and Nigeria naval cooperation partially suppressed attacks; Deep Blue initiative enforcement intermittent; offshore rigs remain at risk.

events.title: Libya: Central Mediterranean departure hub
events.summary: Libya remains primary departure point for Central Med crossings; Libyan Coast Guard intercepts funded by EU; detention centres document systematic abuse.
events.whatHappened: EU-funded LYCG intercepts returned thousands; UN reports torture, slavery, rape in detention; parallel UN arms embargo violations continue; western route (Zuwara-Sfax) active.

events.title: English Channel: small boat crossings and UK-France politics
events.summary: Record small-boat crossings from France to UK; Rwanda Policy struck down; UK-France bilateral tension over cost-sharing and returns.
events.whatHappened: Over 30,000 crossings per year; multiple drowning incidents; Rwanda deportation scheme ruled unlawful; UK-France agreement on joint patrols repeatedly tested; Calais camps cleared and reformed.

events.title: Aegean: Greece-Turkey maritime pushbacks
events.summary: Greek coast guard conducts systematic pushbacks into Turkish waters documented by human rights monitors; Frontex complicit findings.
events.whatHappened: Hellenic Coast Guard abandons boats mid-sea; ECHR rulings against Greece; Frontex suspended operations then resumed with reforms; Turkey instrumentalises crossings during diplomatic disputes.

events.title: Darién Gap: record crossings into North America
events.summary: Record 520,000+ crossings through the Darién jungle in 2023; Ecuadorian and Venezuelan nationals majority; criminal network control of routes.
events.whatHappened: Multiple nationalities cross dangerous rainforest route; Clan del Golfo and FARC dissidents charge transit fees; Panama builds reception centres; US pressures Colombia on interdiction.

events.title: Canary Islands: West African Atlantic route
events.summary: Atlantic route from Senegal, Mauritania and Morocco to Canary Islands; record arrivals 2023-24; high mortality in open ocean passages.
events.whatHappened: Cayucos carry hundreds across 1,400km open Atlantic; rescue operations overwhelmed; Spain-Senegal cooperation agreements on returns contested; record deaths per crossing ratio.

events.title: Belarus-Poland: hybrid migration as geopolitical weapon
events.summary: Lukashenko regime facilitates migration pressure on Poland as retaliation for EU sanctions; Poland constructs 187km border barrier.
events.whatHappened: Migrants from Iraq, Syria, Afghanistan flown to Minsk, directed to border; Polish state-of-emergency zone bans journalists; deaths in forest documented by Ocalenie Foundation; barrier completed 2022.

events.title: Tunisia: Sfax becomes primary departure point
events.summary: Sfax overtook Zuwara as primary Central Med departure point after Saied anti-migration decrees; EU-Tunisia MoU funds coast guard expansion.
events.whatHappened: Tunisian authorities expelled thousands of Sub-Saharan Africans to desert border; EU €105m deal condemned by rights groups; UNHCR access restricted; Sfax crossings surge.

events.title: Rohingya: Bay of Bengal sea crossings continue
events.summary: Rohingya refugees from Bangladesh camps undertake dangerous Andaman Sea crossings to Malaysia and Indonesia; maritime pushbacks widespread.
events.whatHappened: Boats intercepted by Thai, Malaysian and Indonesian navies; UNHCR reports thousands in peril; trafficking networks exploit camp overcrowding in Cox's Bazar; repatriation to Myanmar stalled.

events.title: Horn of Africa: conflict displacement and migration flows
events.summary: Tigray war aftermath and ongoing instability drive displacement through the Horn; Sudan civil war closes traditional refuge.
events.whatHappened: Post-Tigray IDP returns stalled; Eritrean refugees in Ethiopia and Sudan face camp closures; new displacement from Amhara and Sudan war adds to regional crisis; routes to Libya active.

events.title: Nord Stream pipelines: sabotage and geopolitical fallout
events.summary: Nord Stream 1 and 2 explosions in September 2022 destroyed European gas infrastructure; investigations ongoing; geopolitical blame contested.
events.whatHappened: Four pipeline sections ruptured; Germany and Sweden investigations closed or stalled citing state actor complexity; US, Russia, Ukraine all named in conflicting investigations; European gas market permanently altered.

events.title: BTC pipeline: Caspian oil corridor and geopolitics
events.summary: BTC pipeline carries Azerbaijani crude through Georgia to Turkish Mediterranean port; key route bypassing Russia and Iran.
events.whatHappened: Azerbaijan-Armenia war 2020 and 2023 raised sabotage risk; pipeline bypasses Russian and Iranian territory; Turkey's Ceyhan terminal strategic for EU energy diversification from Russia.

events.title: East Mediterranean gas: contested EEZ and energy diplomacy
events.summary: Aphrodite, Leviathan, Zohr and other fields contested between Cyprus, Israel, Lebanon, Turkey and Egypt; EEZ boundary disputes unsettled.
events.whatHappened: Israeli Leviathan gas increasingly exported to Egypt and Europe; Lebanon-Israel maritime deal (2022) allowed Karish development; Turkey-Libya MoU contests Greek and Cypriot EEZs.

events.title: Arctic LNG-2: sanctions freeze Russian mega-project
events.summary: US and EU sanctions targeting equipment suppliers stalled Arctic LNG-2 project; Western contractors withdrew; Chinese and Indian buyers hesitant.
events.whatHappened: Novatek's $21bn project halted by sanctions on specialised modules; tanker fleet unable to source ice-class vessels under Western classification; first LNG deliveries delayed by years.

events.title: Mozambique LNG: Total Energies and insurgency
events.summary: Total Energies declared force majeure after 2021 Palma attack; partial security restoration by Rwanda forces; project restart timelines uncertain.
events.whatHappened: $20bn LNG project suspended; RWANDAN forces and SAMIM partially secure perimeter; Total assessing restart; Eni's Coral South FLNG vessel producing but onshore project stalled.

events.title: Saudi Aramco / OPEC+: production cuts and oil politics
events.summary: Saudi Arabia leads OPEC+ production cuts to maintain oil price floor; US diplomatic tension over energy policy and Israel-Gaza war.
events.whatHappened: Voluntary cuts of 1–2 mb/d maintained through 2024-25; Saudi-Russia coordination on OPEC+ persists despite Ukraine war; US-Saudi relations strained over Gaza refusal to normalise with Israel.

events.title: US: Permian Basin shale dominance reshapes global markets
events.summary: US remains world's largest oil and gas producer; record LNG exports replace Russian gas in Europe; geopolitical weight of American energy abundance.
events.whatHappened: US LNG exports to Europe doubled post-Nord Stream; Permian output exceeds 6 mb/d; Biden IRA investments and Trump reversal create policy uncertainty; LNG export terminals expand on Gulf coast.

events.title: China: APT cyber operations — global espionage campaigns
events.summary: Salt Typhoon and Volt Typhoon APT groups attributed to Chinese state compromised US telecom networks, critical infrastructure and government systems.
events.whatHappened: Salt Typhoon breached AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile for political intelligence; Volt Typhoon pre-positioned in US power and water utilities; NSA and CISA issued emergency advisories; FBI attribution contested by Beijing.

events.title: US: Section 702 FISA reauthorisation — bulk surveillance expanded
events.summary: Congress reauthorised and expanded Section 702 FISA collection in April 2024; new provisions allow broader data broker access without warrant.
events.whatHappened: Expanded authority allows NSA collection from US data brokers; civil liberties coalition opposition defeated; non-US persons subject to warrantless collection; Snowden precedent ignored.

events.title: Pegasus spyware: MENA governments target journalists
events.summary: NSO Group's Pegasus deployed by Saudi Arabia, UAE, Morocco, India and others against journalists, activists and political opponents.
events.whatHappened: Citizen Lab and Access Now documented hundreds of targets; Khashoggi associates targeted before his murder; EU Parliament investigation inconclusive; NSO blacklisted by US but still operational.

events.title: EU AI Act: enforcement begins for high-risk systems
events.summary: EU AI Act entered force August 2024; prohibited practices ban takes effect February 2025; biometric surveillance and social scoring restricted.
events.whatHappened: First prohibited-practice rules in force; high-risk system compliance deadlines staggered through 2026-27; GPAI model rules apply to frontier labs; enforcement infrastructure under construction.

events.title: Huawei Marine: undersea cable exclusion campaigns
events.summary: US campaigns to exclude Huawei Marine Networks from cable projects globally; cables as infrastructure for intelligence collection.
events.whatHappened: US Embassy cables advise partners against Huawei cable contracts; SubCom and Alcatel-Lucent alternatives subsidised; AfricaConnect routes contested; landing station backdoor allegations unproven.

events.title: Turkey: Bayraktar drone exports reshape battlefield access
events.summary: Bayraktar TB2 and Akıncı drones exported to Ukraine, Ethiopia, Morocco, Niger and others; Turkish drone diplomacy reshapes conflict dynamics.
events.whatHappened: TB2 proved decisive in Libya, Nagorno-Karabakh, Ukraine; Baykar exports to 26+ countries; Kızılelma autonomous UCAV in development; US and EU allies express concern over spread.

events.title: AI targeting systems: Lavender and Gospel in Gaza
events.summary: IDF AI targeting systems Lavender and Gospel reportedly generated thousands of strike targets in Gaza with minimal human review.
events.whatHappened: +972 Magazine investigation revealed Lavender assigned casualty scores to 37,000 Palestinian men; Gospel generated building strike lists; human oversight reportedly reduced to seconds per target.

events.title: US: Ukraine military aid packages and congressional battles
events.summary: US provided $75bn+ in military assistance to Ukraine 2022-26; HIMARS, Abrams, Patriot, F-16s transferred amid Congressional MAGA blockades.
events.whatHappened: Aid packages repeatedly delayed by House Republican obstruction; $61bn April 2024 package finally passed; F-16 deliveries from Netherlands and Denmark; long-range ATACMS allowed for strikes inside Russia.

events.title: Germany: Taurus cruise missile supply debated for Ukraine
events.summary: Scholz government repeatedly refused to supply Taurus cruise missiles to Ukraine citing escalation risk and German targeting role requirements.
events.whatHappened: Taurus capable of striking Crimea bridge and Russian logistics; Scholz declined citing requirement for German soldiers to be involved in targeting; intercepted Bundeswehr call revealed planning discussion; coalition split.

events.title: Iran: Shahed drone transfers to Russia and proxies
events.summary: Iran transferred thousands of Shahed-136 kamikaze drones to Russia for use against Ukrainian infrastructure; also supplies Houthi and Hezbollah arsenals.
events.whatHappened: Shaheds used to strike Ukrainian power grid nightly; EU and US sanctions on Iranian drone producers and ships; Iran established drone factory in Russia (Alabuga); transfers to Yemen via Omani waters.

events.title: North Korea: ammunition and missile transfers to Russia
events.summary: North Korea transferred millions of artillery shells and ballistic missiles to Russia; Kim-Putin summit September 2023 formalised cooperation.
events.whatHappened: Ship-to-ship transfers documented via satellite imagery; US intelligence estimates millions of 152mm shells; KN-23 ballistic missiles used in Ukraine strikes; DPRK troops deployed to Russia in late 2024.

events.title: South Korea: global arms export surge
events.summary: South Korea emerged as top-5 global arms exporter; K2 tanks, K9 howitzers and FA-50 jets sold to Poland, Romania, Australia, UAE.
events.whatHappened: Korean defence industry capitalises on NATO member rearmament demand; $17bn Polish framework contract largest in Korean export history; co-production deals in Poland and Australia negotiated.

events.title: Czech artillery: 800,000 shell initiative for Ukraine
events.summary: Czech initiative to procure 800,000 155mm shells outside EU for Ukraine; Canada, Denmark and others co-funded; first deliveries summer 2024.
events.whatHappened: Czech PM Fiala led extra-EU sourcing effort; shells from South Africa, Turkey, India identified; Canada contributed €21m; first 180,000 shells delivered by July 2024.

events.title: UK Storm Shadow: cruise missile supply to Ukraine
events.summary: UK became first NATO member to supply long-range cruise missiles to Ukraine; Storm Shadow strikes on Crimea and Black Sea targets followed.
events.whatHappened: Storm Shadow strikes on Crimean bridge, Kerch approaches and Sevastopol navy base; Russia expelled UK ambassador; France also supplied SCALP EG variant; range ~250km.

events.title: Egypt: canal revenue crisis and IMF programme
events.summary: Egypt secured $8bn IMF programme March 2024 after canal revenues collapsed; currency devalued 35%; Gulf sovereign wealth funds injected capital.
events.whatHappened: IMF deal conditioned on FX liberalisation; EGP devalued from 30 to 50 per USD; Saudi, Emirati and Qatari investments in Ras El-Hekma and utilities secured balance of payments.

events.title: GERD dam: Ethiopia-Egypt-Sudan Nile water war
events.summary: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam nearly operational; Egypt views as existential threat to Nile water security; negotiations deadlocked since 2021.
events.whatHappened: GERD 4th filling completed 2024; Egypt declares 'no compromise' on historic water share; Sudan position oscillated; US mediation failed 2020; African Union facilitated talks inconclusive.

events.title: Istanbul: Kanal Istanbul mega-project and Montreux stakes
events.summary: Kanal Istanbul would bypass Bosphorus but also bypass Montreux Convention; military and commercial implications contested.
events.whatHappened: Project approved 2021; environmental opposition strong; cost estimates $15bn+; would allow warships to bypass Montreux limits; Russia implicitly favours; NATO uneasy; construction pace slow.

events.title: Kiel Canal: Germany's critical waterway needs €10bn renovation
events.summary: Germany's Kiel Canal busiest artificial waterway globally; lock infrastructure aged; NATO military transit needs and commercial shipping both at risk.
events.whatHappened: Federal government acknowledges €10bn+ renovation gap; lock chambers dating to 1914 failing; Baltic Sea NATO operations require reliable transit; funding approved but timeline decade-plus.

events.title: Frontex: surveillance and pushback infrastructure in Med
events.summary: Frontex operates Heron drones and patrol vessels across Mediterranean; accused of aiding illegal pushbacks; budget grew from €6m to €900m+.
events.whatHappened: OLAF investigation 2022 found Frontex complicit in pushbacks; director Leggeri resigned; Palma document confirmed aerial surveillance supporting Greek coast guard returns; Eurosur data sharing with Libya.

events.title: India-Bangladesh: border fence and BSF shootings
events.summary: Indian BSF guards shoot and kill Bangladeshi nationals at border routinely; 3,000+ deaths documented since 2000; fencing nearly complete.
events.whatHappened: Barbed wire fence nearly complete along 4,000km; shoot-to-kill orders disputed by India but documented by Odhikar and Human Rights Watch; Rohingya deportations complicate bilateral relations.

events.title: Evros River: Greece-Turkey border militarisation
events.summary: 40km concrete barrier and surveillance technology deployed along Evros; systematic pushbacks into Meriç documented; deaths in river.
events.whatHappened: EU funded 40km concrete wall completed 2023; night-vision surveillance towers; Greek authorities documented stripping and abandoning migrants mid-river; ECHR interim measures ignored.

events.title: Colombia-Venezuela: closed border and smuggling economy
events.summary: Closed formal crossings push 7 million Venezuelan migrants through trochas controlled by armed groups; normalisation under Petro-Maduro rapprochement partial.
events.whatHappened: Formal crossings partially reopened 2022 under Petro; ELN and colectivos control informal crossings; fuel, food and drug smuggling economics dominate border zones; UNHCR monitors deportations.

events.title: Ceuta and Melilla: Morocco-Spain border violence
events.summary: Morocco periodically opens border as diplomatic pressure; mass crossing events; Spain-Morocco relations tied to Western Sahara recognition.
events.whatHappened: May 2021 mass crossing crisis (10,000 in 48h) followed Spanish hosting of Polisario leader; Spain subsequently recognised Moroccan autonomy plan for Western Sahara; EU funds Morocco border management.

events.title: Australia: offshore detention and Pacific push policy
events.summary: Offshore detention on Nauru and PNG for boat arrivals; Operation Sovereign Borders intercepts vessels; UNHCR access denied; decades-long legal limbo.
events.whatHappened: Albanese government maintained naval turnbacks; NZYQ case forced release of stateless detainees; offshore cohort reduced but policy remains; reports of abuse and self-harm on Nauru.

events.title: Ukraine: systematic destruction of power infrastructure
events.summary: Russia's systematic missile and drone campaign against Ukrainian power infrastructure has destroyed 80%+ of generation capacity; winter blackouts affect millions.
events.whatHappened: Repeated waves of Shahed drone and missile strikes target thermal power plants, transformer stations and substations; Ukraine's energy industry association estimates $56bn in damage; EU provides generators and equipment.

events.title: TSMC and Taiwan: semiconductor chokepoint
events.summary: TSMC manufactures 90%+ of world's most advanced chips; Taiwan conflict scenarios trigger global semiconductor collapse planning.
events.whatHappened: US CHIPS Act subsidises TSMC Arizona fab; Samsung Korea and Intel Ohio as contingency; TSMC Arizona fabs face yield and workforce challenges; Taiwan invasion scenario triggers NATO war-game chip-supply scenarios.

events.title: Baltimore Key Bridge: collapse closes major US port
events.summary: Container ship Dali struck Francis Scott Key Bridge; bridge collapsed; six workers killed; Baltimore channel closed months; auto import disruption.
events.whatHappened: MV Dali power failure caused collision March 26, 2024; channel re-opened to commercial traffic June 2024 after controlled demolition; auto manufacturers rerouted through Northeast ports.

events.title: Sahel: telecommunications breakdown under military rule
events.summary: Military juntas in Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso use systematic internet shutdowns during operations; French telecom companies withdraw; infrastructure deteriorates.
events.whatHappened: Orange and Airtel operations disrupted or expelled; Orange Mali forced divestment; Starlink filling gaps but juntas restrict access; shutdown duration during military ops extended to days.

events.title: Germany: energy crisis-driven deindustrialisation
events.summary: High energy costs post-Russia gas cutoff accelerate German industrial relocation; BASF, Thyssenkrupp and automakers restructure or offshore production.
events.whatHappened: German gas prices remained 3–4x pre-war levels; BASF Ludwigshafen investment halved, China operations expanded; Volkswagen and BMW announce German plant closures; GDP decline unique among G7.

events.title: Amazon: deforestation legal Amazon and Lula reversals
events.summary: Lula's 2023 comeback reversed Bolsonaro-era deforestation surge; PRODES data shows 50% drop; cerrado and other biomes less protected.
events.whatHappened: 2023-24 deforestation in Legal Amazon fell to decade lows; Lula signed zero-deforestation decrees; but cerrado clearing accelerated; fires still record in 2024 drought; arc of deforestation frontier active.

events.title: East Africa: multi-year drought and food crisis
events.summary: Worst multi-year drought in 40 years hit Horn of Africa 2020-23; partial rains followed by floods; cyclical La Niña-El Niño swings amplify extremes.
events.whatHappened: 22 million at risk of starvation at peak; failed rains in five consecutive seasons in Somalia, Kenya, Ethiopia; IPC Phase 4-5 conditions; 2023-24 El Niño floods then renewed drought.

events.title: Greece: record wildfires — Dadia, Alexandroupoli 2023
events.summary: 2023 Dadia fire largest in EU recorded history; 96,000 ha burned in Thrace; Mediterranean fire season extending into autumn annually.
events.whatHappened: Arsonist fires and lightning converged on tinder-dry Dadia forest; 96,000+ hectares; 21 dead migrants found in fire zone; EU Copernicus EFFIS records Greece as multi-year fire hotspot.

events.title: Arctic sea ice: record minimum and navigation opening
events.summary: September 2023 Arctic sea ice minimum hit record low; multi-year ice disappearing; permafrost thaw accelerating methane release.
events.whatHappened: Sea ice extent fell to 1.63 million km²; NSR ice-free window extends; permafrost thaw releasing stored methane at increasing rates; Greenland ice sheet mass loss accelerates.

events.title: Sahara expansion: desertification and the Sahel dryline
events.summary: Sahara expanding southward; Great Green Wall project 4% complete; dust storms intensify over Mediterranean and Atlantic; arable land lost annually.
events.whatHappened: UNCCD reports 23 ha of arable land lost per minute globally; Sahara southern boundary advanced ~48km south since 1920; Great Green Wall 8,000km target at 4% completion by 2023.

events.title: Pakistan: catastrophic monsoon floods, 2022 and recurrence
events.summary: 2022 floods submerged one-third of Pakistan; $30bn damage; annual flooding worsens as glaciers melt and monsoon intensifies.
events.whatHappened: 33 million affected; 1,700+ killed; Sindh and Balochistan hardest hit; Indus glacial melt adds to monsoon volume; reconstruction incomplete when 2023 floods arrived; climate debt framing in COP debates.

events.title: Colorado River: dead pool scenarios and water wars
events.summary: Lake Mead and Powell at historic lows 2021-23; US states reach temporary cuts deal; long-term overallocation unresolved.
events.whatHappened: Mead fell to 27% capacity 2022; Bureau of Reclamation declared Tier 2 shortage; Arizona, Nevada and Mexico took cuts; 2023-24 rains partial recovery; overallocation by 3 million acre-feet annual unresolved.

events.title: Great Barrier Reef: mass bleaching events accelerate
events.summary: 2024 bleaching event most extensive in GBR history; 5th mass bleaching event in 8 years; UNESCO critical danger listing resisted by Australia.
events.whatHappened: GBRMPA reports 73% of reefs surveyed showed bleaching in 2024; El Niño sea temperature +2°C above average; Australia lobbied successfully against UNESCO danger listing but committed new funds.

events.title: Starlink: commercial satcom as military backbone
events.summary: SpaceX Starlink became backbone of Ukrainian military communications; Musk's political restrictions sparked crisis; US Starshield for military clients.
events.whatHappened: 40,000+ terminals in Ukraine; Musk cut coverage to prevent Crimea drone attack; US government purchased Starshield commercial satellite service; Russia unable to jam effectively at scale.

events.title: China: Yaogan military reconnaissance satellites
events.summary: China's Yaogan constellation of 80+ military satellites provides persistent surveillance coverage; SAR satellites monitor US carrier groups.
events.whatHappened: Yaogan-39, -40, -41 triplet launches increase coverage frequency; commercial Planet and BlackSky imagery used to verify movements; PLA denies military use; US tracks Yaogan for carrier group monitoring.

events.title: Russia: GLONASS and electronic warfare dominance
events.summary: Russia deploys Murmansk-BN and Krasukha electronic warfare systems to jam GPS and disrupt drone navigation over Ukraine and Baltic.
events.whatHappened: Baltic flights report GPS interference from Kaliningrad and Russia; Ukrainian drones rely on alternative navigation after GPS jamming; GLONASS-denied operations force tactical adaptation; Finland documents jamming.

events.title: Iran: Noor military satellite programme
events.summary: IRGC Aerospace Force launched Noor-1, -2, -3 military satellites; US intelligence doubts full surveillance capability but orbit establishes precedent.
events.whatHappened: Noor-3 launched 2023; IRGC claims to monitor military movements; US and Israeli analysts assess limited actual ISR capability but political signal strong; Iran joins exclusive military satellite club.

events.title: EU Galileo: satellite navigation sovereignty
events.summary: EU Galileo PRS encrypted signal available to member state military users; Europe seeks GPS independence; third-generation satellites in development.
events.whatHappened: Galileo Full Operational Capability achieved; PRS (Public Regulated Service) for government security users activated; EU pushes member states to adopt Galileo over GPS in military procurement.

events.title: SpaceX Starshield: Pentagon's dedicated satellite tier
events.summary: SpaceX's Starshield provides NRO and DoD classified satellite communications; separates US military from commercial Starlink dependency.
events.whatHappened: Starshield contract with NRO worth $1.8bn+; classified payloads and government-encrypted comms; Ukrainean government purchases separate from commercial Starlink; allies access under arrangement.

events.title: ICC: arrest warrants for Gaza — Netanyahu, Sinwar, Hamas
events.summary: ICC Prosecutor Karim Khan sought arrest warrants for Netanyahu, Gallant and Hamas leaders for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza.
events.whatHappened: Pre-trial chamber issued warrants November 2024; US Congress threatened ICC with sanctions; UK, France, Germany queried legal process; ICC jurisdiction contested by Israel and US; Canada and Netherlands indicated compliance.

events.title: UN Security Council: Russia veto deadlock on Ukraine
events.summary: Russia has vetoed 20+ UNSC resolutions on Ukraine; China abstains on most; Uniting for Peace mechanism used to bypass Security Council.
events.whatHappened: UNSC paralysis on Ukraine, Gaza; UNGA emergency special sessions voted large majorities condemning Russia; General Assembly Uniting for Peace resolution passed 2023; US vetoed Gaza ceasefire resolutions.

events.title: EU: 13 packages of Russia sanctions — architecture and evasion
events.summary: EU enacted 13 sanctions packages against Russia; oil price cap, SWIFT exclusions, asset freezes; evasion through third countries well-documented.
events.whatHappened: G7 oil price cap at $60; Russia reroutes through UAE, Turkey, India; SWIFT disconnected for listed banks but alternatives found; frozen €300bn in central bank assets debate on use for Ukraine reconstruction.

events.title: SIPRI 2025 report: arms spending at Cold War record
events.summary: SIPRI 2025 yearbook documents global military spending at $2.24 trillion — highest since Cold War; Europe increases fastest.
events.whatHappened: NATO Europe up 17% in real terms; Germany, Poland at or near 2% GDP target; Middle East +9%; Russia+34%; China +6%; global total up 6.8%; aid to Ukraine accounts for substantial share.

events.title: NATO: Baltic and Eastern flank reinforcement
events.summary: NATO activated enhanced forward presence in Baltic states and Poland; Finland and Sweden joined; permanent basing replacing rotation discussed.
events.whatHappened: Finland joined 2023; Sweden joined 2024; NATO deployed German-led brigade to Lithuania permanently; US 101st Airborne returned to Europe; defence spending pledges at 2%+ GDP for most members.

events.title: G7: €300bn Russian frozen assets and loan-for-Ukraine scheme
events.summary: G7 agreed to use interest from €300bn frozen Russian assets to underwrite $50bn loan to Ukraine; legal and seizure debates ongoing.
events.whatHappened: Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration (ERA) loans of $50bn approved June 2024 Puglia G7; interest on frozen Euroclear assets (~€3bn/year) used for debt service; Russia threatens retaliatory asset seizures.
